identity.title: Visual Planning: Let's Think Only with Images

problem.claim: Reasoning and planning for tasks involving spatial or geometrical information may be better supported by visual representations than by language alone.

gap.claim: Existing multimodal models predominantly express and structure reasoning in text, even when visual information is present.

contributions.claim: Visual Planning performs planning through image sequences that encode step-by-step visual inference, supplementing language-based reasoning.
VPRL uses GRPO to post-train large vision models for visual planning.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors introduce Visual Planning as a purely visual planning paradigm for vision-first tasks.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report substantial planning improvements from VPRL on FrozenLake, Maze, and MiniBehavior.
The authors report that Visual Planning outperforms other planning variants that reason only in text.

narrative_sequence.summary: Recent LLM and MLLM advances have improved machine reasoning, but reasoning remains predominantly text-based.
The authors argue that language is not always the natural or effective modality for spatial and geometrical reasoning.
They propose Visual Planning: image sequences encode step-by-step planning in the visual domain as a supplementary reasoning channel.
They introduce VPRL with GRPO and report improvements across three visual navigation tasks, plus an advantage over text-only planning variants.

source_observation.claim: The abstract aligns a modality-specific limitation with a modality-specific intervention: text-dominant reasoning is followed by image-sequence planning for spatial tasks.

lessons.interpretation: A paper can make its motivation more concrete by matching the representation used by the method to the structure of the target task.
lessons.application: For a task with explicit spatial structure, define an intermediate representation that preserves that structure and describe how it supports stepwise inference.
lessons.exception: This move may be unsuitable when the task’s essential information is primarily linguistic or when visual representations cannot compactly encode the needed reasoning.

unknowns: The abstract does not report dataset sizes, baselines beyond the broad text-only comparison, numerical gains, statistical uncertainty, or task-specific conditions.
It does not clarify whether Visual Planning is evaluated alone, jointly with language reasoning, or under comparable computational budgets.
